# Benchmark results

Measured 26 October 2026 with the tools in [README.md](README.md).

**Machine:** Intel Core Ultra 7 265KF (20 threads), 32 GB RAM, NVMe SSD, Windows 11 Pro 26200.
**Apps:** Quarry 0.1.0 (release build), Notepad++ 8.9.8.1 (64-bit), UltraEdit 33.0.0.23,
VS Code 1.143.1 (fresh profile, extensions disabled). All with default settings, except that the
"open anyway?" prompts were answered automatically (see below).
**Files:** generated by `bench/gen.mjs`, read with a warm file cache (see the caveats in the README),
except in [Cold file cache](#cold-file-cache) below.

## Quarry, Notepad++ and UltraEdit (`bench/native.ps1`)

Same script and launch for all three. **Title** = the window title shows the file name.
**Loaded** = the app has also stopped reading from disk for 1 s. **Memory** = private memory of
all the app's processes, 3 s after loading.

| File | Quarry | Notepad++ | UltraEdit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1-line file (baseline) | 0.49 s, 321 MB | **0.29 s / 0.68 s, 67 MB** | 1.41 s / 1.80 s, 705 MB |
| 1 GB log | **0.48 s, 431 MB** | 1.18 s / 1.27 s, 1.2 GB | 2.06 s / 2.74 s, 729 MB ¹ |
| 1 GB JSON | **0.48 s, 403 MB** | 1.73 s / 2.31 s, 1.6 GB | 2.08 s / 2.70 s, 747 MB ¹ |
| 5 GB log | **0.47 s, 427 MB** | 5.77 s / 6.32 s, 5.7 GB ² | 2.05 s / 4.36 s, 741 MB ¹ |
| 5 GB JSON | **0.48 s, 447 MB** | 8.75 s / 9.02 s, 7.8 GB ² | 2.11 s / 5.03 s, 753 MB ¹ |

Times are *title / loaded*. Quarry reads through a memory mapping (Windows doesn't count those as
disk reads), so its two times are the same: the moment its first screen of text is up. It then
indexes the rest in the background (3.6 s for the 5 GB log, see the engine table) while the file
is already usable.

¹ UltraEdit asked about **temporary file handling** for every file over 50 MB; the default answer
("disable temporary files for files over 50 MB, this session only") was taken.
² Notepad++ warned **"Opening a huge file of 2GB+ could take several minutes. Do you want to open
it?"**; the default answer (Yes) was taken.

## Quarry and VS Code (`bench/app.mjs`)

Time from launch until the file's first line is drawn in the page (both are Chromium-based, so
this is measured inside the page), and private memory once open.

| File | Quarry | VS Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1-line file (baseline) | 0.56 s, 312 MB | 1.39 s, 1.3 GB |
| 100 MB log | 0.66 s, 363 MB | 2.07 s, 1.8 GB |
| 1 GB log | 0.54 s, 411 MB | 5.1–5.2 s, 2.7–2.9 GB ³ |
| 1 GB JSON | 0.54 s, 397 MB | 8.6 s, 3.1 GB ³ |
| 5 GB log | 0.48–0.50 s, 421 MB | 31 s, 8.0 GB ³ |
| 5 GB JSON | 0.55 s, 485 MB | 30 s, 9.0 GB ³ |

³ VS Code asks for confirmation before opening a local file over 1024 MB; the prompt was turned
off for these runs. It also turns off tokenization, wrapping, folding, word highlighting and more
for files this size.

## What the numbers say

- **Opening:** Quarry shows a large file in about half a second whatever its size. The others take
  longer as files grow: UltraEdit about 2 s, Notepad++ and VS Code many seconds at 5 GB.
- **Memory:** Quarry and UltraEdit stay flat as files grow (both read from disk as needed). Notepad++
  holds about the file's size in memory and VS Code about 1.6 times its size.
- **Small files:** Notepad++ starts faster than Quarry (0.29 s vs 0.49 s) and uses far less memory
  (67 MB vs 321 MB). Most of Quarry's memory is the WebView2 engine that draws its interface.
- **Prompts:** Quarry opens every file without asking; each of the others asks once files get big.
- **Features differ:** Quarry's [large-file mode](../docs/large-files.md) has fewer features than its
  normal tabs (for example, no multi-cursor or formatting), and the others turn features off on big
  files too. These tables time opening; they don't compare what you can do once a file is open.

## Quarry's large-file engine (`examples/bench.rs`, no UI)

| | 1 GB log | 5 GB log | 5 GB JSON | 5 GB CSV |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First screen ready | 23 ms | 49 ms | 69 ms | 51 ms |
| Full line index | 0.33 s (11.8 M lines) | 3.6 s (59 M lines) | 4.6 s (321 M lines) | 3.4 s (57 M lines) |
| Jump to the middle line | < 1 ms | < 1 ms | < 1 ms | < 1 ms |
| Find a rare string | 94 ms | 0.50 s | 0.48 s | 0.67 s |
| Find a common word | 0.12 s | 0.39 s | 0.51 s | 0.50 s |
| Find a regex | 0.18 s | 0.67 s | 0.56 s | 1.4 s |
| Replace All (rare string) | 0.44 s | 2.5 s | 2.3 s | 2.4 s |
| Save to a copy | 0.68 s | 4.2 s | 4.9 s | 4.0 s |
| Private memory while open | 3 MB | 12 MB | 11 MB | 12 MB |

**Filter view** (`log-1G.log` / `log-5G.log`):

| | 1 GB log | 5 GB log |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keep the ERROR lines | 0.12 s (1.5 M lines) | 0.63 s (7.4 M lines) |
| Hide the DEBUG lines | 0.17 s (8.9 M lines) | 0.96 s (44 M lines) |
| Peak private memory | 8 MB | 25 MB |

**JSON in large-file mode** (`json-1G.json` / `json-5G.json`):

| | 1 GB JSON | 5 GB JSON |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JSON: Validate (whole file) | 1.0 s | 5.8 s |
| Tree: open the root, list 200 children, expand one record | 0.1 ms | 0.1 ms |
| Tree: count every top-level item (background) | 1.2 s (4,048,616) | 7.1 s (20,079,290) |

## Cold file cache

Measured 26 October 2026 right after a reboot, with the same tools and settings. Each app got its
own copy of each file that nothing had read since the reboot, so every number below is a first read
from the SSD. One run per file.

| File | Quarry | Notepad++ | UltraEdit | VS Code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 GB log | **0.49 s, 400 MB** | 1.60 s / 1.75 s, 1.2 GB | 3.28 s / 3.76 s, 736 MB ⁴ | 6.0 s, 2.8 GB |
| 5 GB log | **0.46 s, 436 MB** | 5.60 s / 5.94 s, 5.7 GB ² | 1.93 s / 4.46 s, 743 MB ¹ | 29.7 s, 8.0 GB ³ |
| 5 GB JSON | **0.45 s, 435 MB** | 9.10 s / 9.45 s, 7.8 GB ² | 1.92 s / 4.38 s, 759 MB ¹ | 29.7 s, 9.0 GB ³ |

Quarry, Notepad++ and UltraEdit: `bench/native.ps1`, *title / loaded*, memory 3 s after loading.
VS Code: `bench/app.mjs`, text on screen, memory 5 s later. The same prompts as above were answered.

⁴ The first UltraEdit run after the reboot also loaded UltraEdit itself from a cold cache; its two
later runs (5 GB) are the fairer comparison.

**Engine** (`examples/bench.rs`) on cold copies. Only the first full pass (the line index) reads
the file cold; the steps after it find the file cached, as they would in the app.

| | 1 GB log | 5 GB log | 5 GB JSON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First screen ready | 47 ms | 51 ms | 74 ms |
| Full line index | 0.62 s | 3.7 s | 4.7 s |
| Find a rare string | 86 ms | 0.48 s | 0.60 s |
| Replace All (rare string) | 0.42 s | 3.0 s | 2.4 s |
| Save to a copy | 0.73 s | 3.7 s | 13.3 s ⁵ |
| Private memory while open | 3 MB | 12 MB | 13 MB |

⁵ Slower than the warm run (4.9 s); this save wrote 5 GB while the cold copies were filling the
file cache, so it is likely limited by the disk and the cache rather than Quarry. Not investigated.

**What changes when the cache is cold:** almost nothing at these sizes on this NVMe SSD. Quarry
still shows the file in under 0.5 s, because it maps the file and reads only the first screen
before showing it; its first-screen time roughly doubles for the 1 GB log (23 → 47 ms) and the 1 GB
line index takes 0.62 s instead of 0.33 s, while the 5 GB index (3.7 s) was already limited by
reading the file. Notepad++ and VS Code read the whole file either way: a little slower at 1 GB
(Notepad++ 1.18 → 1.60 s, VS Code 5.1 → 6.0 s) and about the same as warm at 5 GB, as is UltraEdit. A slower disk (SATA SSD, hard disk, network share) would widen every gap that depends on
reading the whole file, and would slow Quarry's background indexing too, not its first screen.

## Not yet measured

- Search, Replace All and Save in the other editors (only opening is compared so far).
